* make a new "language" called Android and put the instrumentations in there, acknowledging in advance that android isn't a language.

comments.body:
Hello there! 👋  I thought I'd add my two cents since I am familiar with the LFX platform in my role as tech lead for TAG Operational Resilience. 
The good news is that LFX has a CLI, which you can easily run a command to get the meeting recording links. The CLI is a generic authenticated API client, so it's not as intuitive as `lfx meetings list`.
The Swagger UI is available at https://lfx-api.v2.cluster.lfx.dev/docs/
The OpenAPI document is /docs/spec/openapi-merged.yaml
The relevant OpenAPI document is `/docs/spec/openapi-merged.yaml`
Download it:
```bash
lfx api /docs/spec/openapi-merged.yaml > openapi.yaml
```
Find meeting and project paths:
```bash
yq -r '
  .paths | keys[] |
  select(test("(?i)meeting|record|project"))
' openapi.yaml
```
The important API paths are:
```bash
/query/resources
/itx/meeting_count
/itx/meetings/{meeting_id}
/itx/past_meetings/{past_meeting_id}
```
The important discovery endpoint is `GET /query/resources`And its required parameter is `v=1`. Its name search parameter is `name=`.
So, the correct command is:
```bash
lfx api \
  '/query/resources?v=1&name=OpenTelemetry&page_size=100' \
  > resources.json
```
The endpoint’s relevant parameters include:
- `v`, required API version, use `1`.
- `name`, resource name or alias.
- `parent`, optional parent such as `project:PROJECT_UID`.
- `type`, optional resource type.
- `sort`, such as `best_match` or `updated_desc`.
- `page_size`, from 1 to 1000.

fatiando/harmonica#586.title: harmonica.reduction_to_pole  flipping the output in north-south
fatiando/harmonica#586.body:
Using harmonica.reduction_to_pole (v 0.7.0) with input TMI data read from an ERmapper ERS grid to an xarray. Data is in the north hemisphere in a UTM projection.Plotted input using a matplotlib helper - OK. Pass the xarray to harmonica.reduction_to_pole; plot the output (rtp) with same matplotlib helper). The RTP was computed but the data is flipped north to south. Both data arrays have similar spatial attributes (pasted below). Note that the CRS is dropped in the output. 

[AMF_38N_TestArea_Harmonica.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22538024/AMF_38N_TestArea_Harmonica.zip)

comments.author: santisoler
comments.body:
Hi @fearaschiarrai. Thanks for opening this Issue. I was able to reproduce the bug. I'm leaving here a smaller example that reproduces it, just to make it easier to test in the future. It downloads the [Lightning Creek Sill Complex magnetic grid available in Ensaio](https://www.fatiando.org/ensaio/latest/gallery/lightning-creek-magnetic.html#sphx-glr-gallery-lightning-creek-magnetic-py), flips the northing coordinate and computes the RTP. We can see how the RTP flips the grid as you pointed out.

```python
import numpy as np
import xrft
import xarray as xr
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import ensaio
import harmonica as hm

fname = ensaio.fetch_lightning_creek_magnetic(version=1)

tf = xr.load_dataset(fname).total_field_anomaly

# Flip the northing coordinate in the data array
tf = tf[::-1, :]
print("Total field anomaly grid after flipping the northing coordinate:")
print(tf)

# Pad the grid
pad_width = {
    "easting": tf.easting.size // 3,
    "northing": tf.northing.size // 3,
}
tf_padded = xrft.pad(tf.drop_vars("height"), pad_width)

# Plot padded grid
scale = 0.5 * np.max(np.abs(tf_padded))
tf_padded.plot(vmin=-scale, vmax=scale, cmap="RdBu_r")
plt.gca().set_aspect("equal")
plt.title("Padded TFA grid")
plt.show()

# Compute RTP
inclination, declination = -52.98, 6.51
rtp = hm.reduction_to_pole(tf_padded, inclination=inclination, declination=declination)

# Plot RTP grid
scale = 0.5 * np.max(np.abs(rtp))
rtp.plot(vmin=-scale, vmax=scale, cmap="RdBu_r")
plt.gca().set_asp

GlacioHack/xdem#943.title: Problems with settings for blockwise blocks
GlacioHack/xdem#943.body:
Hello,

While working on the QGIS plugin, I noticed a few strange thing in `blockwise.py`, concerning block sizes.

During the fit the DEM is divided into a grid of tiles and a specific shift is calculated for each tile. Then we extracts the coordinates of the center of each tile and associates them with the calculated shift. Next, these results are fed into the RANSAC, it is designed to model this shift as a single equation.

Currently, the advanced examples in the documentation only use the `chunk_size`. The problem is that the center of the tile will not be calculated based on `chunk_size`, but rather on the `block_size_fit`. The default value of  `block_size_fit` will then be used (500).

line 174 `blockwise.py`
```python
outputs_coreg = map_multiproc_collect(
            self._coreg_wrapper,
            reference_elev,
            self.mp_config,
            to_be_aligned_elev,
            self.procstep,
            inlier_mask,
            return_tile=True,
        )

self.shape_tiling_grid = compute_tiling(
            self.block_size_fit, reference_elev.shape, to_be_aligned_elev.shape
        ).shape
```

The RANSAC therefore receives shifts and coordinates that do not match which invalidates the results.

///

There is another similar issue, this time with the `.apply`.

line 390 `blockwise.py`
```python
self.mp_config.chunk_size = self.block_size_apply
```
Similar situation, if you only specify `chunk_size`, `.apply` will use the default value of `block_size_apply` (500)

///

Currently, best practice is to specify all parameters.
Here is an example:
```python
mp_config = MultiprocConfig(chunk_size=400, outfile="aligned_dem.tif", cluster=None)
blockwise = xdem.coreg.BlockwiseCoreg(xdem.coreg.NuthKaab(), mp_config=mp_config, block_size_fit=400, block_size_apply=800)
```

This solution works, but I find it strange to ask the user to enter the same value twice.
I think it’s possible to make the configuration much simpler.

comments.author: rhugonnet
marinebcht
comments.body: Hi @ould-a We did not have the time to talk this morning about this issue + the BlockwiseCoreg modification. I looked at the first problem you mention. Actually, you're right, in the fit part : 1. we call map_multiproc_collect on the full dem, with the mp_config chunk size to have one coreg / chunk 2. for each of this chunck we compute the center BUT using block_size_fit / 2 and not chunk_size / 2 So yes you can, depending on the values, have some area not covered by the fit in the output coreg blockwize coord info ! Plus, block_size_fit needs to be < chunks_size due to an index error between the chunk grid and the block_size_fit grid.

**Triage notes:**

- **Classification**: Bug (v3, Typescript) — `nameTypeOf()` in modules.ts binding generator is missing `strings.ReplaceAll(tname, "*", "")` which `arrayifyValue()` in App.d.ts already does, causing inconsistent type names for pointer types in generic bindings.

comments.author: leaanthony
comments.body:
Relabelled **v3 → v2**: the affected code is the v2 binding generator (your `wails doctor` also shows v2.12.0). The v3 generator is a different implementation and handles generic pointer params consistently.

Exact root cause for anyone picking this up:

- `v2/internal/binding/generate.go` → `arrayifyValue()` strips `*` **before** mangling generic brackets, producing `main.Message_string_` in `App.d.ts`.
- `v2/internal/typescriptify/typescriptify.go` → `nameTypeOf()` does **not** strip `*`, so `Message[*string]` becomes `Message__string_` in `models.ts` (the `*` turns into a second underscore).

The generated declaration and the reference therefore never match for generic types instantiated with pointer type arguments.

**Fix**: in `nameTypeOf()`, add `tname = strings.ReplaceAll(tname, "*", "")` after `typeOf.Name()` (mirroring `arrayifyValue`), plus a regression test with a `type Message[T any]` instantiated as `Message[*string]` asserting both generators emit `Message_string_`. Marked as a good first issue — happy to review a PR.

wailsapp/wails#5799.title: Expose WebView navigation interception (with URL + cancel) and cookie access API in v3
wailsapp/wails#5799.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

In Wails v3 (v3.0.0-alpha2.117), the WebView is the only way to render a third-party login / SAML / SSO page inside the app. A common auth flow is: open an external auth URL in the WebView → the provider finishes login and redirects to a callback URL that carries a token (e.g. .../callback?token=... or http://localhost:PORT/callback?token=...) → the app must capture that token and close the WebView.

Currently there is no supported way to capture a token delivered via a redirect URL or a cookie from inside the WebView. This blocks two real scenarios:

- Mobile (iOS/Android): the app sandbox forbids binding a localhost port, so a localhost callback listener is impossible. The token must be captured from within the WebView.
- Desktop: without navigation/cookie access, the only fallback is running a localhost listener, which we want to avoid.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a Wails v3 app with a WebView.
2. Load an external URL that, after some interaction, redirects to a custom callback URL containing a token (e.g. myapp://callback?token=abc).
3. Try to detect that navigation from Go/TS to extract the token and stop the navigation.
4. Observe that no public API provides the target URL during navigation, and the only navigation event (WebViewNavigationCompleted) does not include the URL.
5. Alternatively, try to read the WebView's cookies after auth completes — no public cookie API exists.

### Expected behaviour

- A navigation hook that exposes the target URL and allows cancelling the navigation, e.g.
```go
webview.OnNavigationStarting(func(url string) bool {
    if strings.HasPrefix(url, "myapp://callback") {
        token := extract(url)
        return false // cancel
    }
    return true
})
```
- A cookie access API, e.g. webview.GetCookies() / webview.SetCookie(...).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

- Used the internal navigationStarting handler — it exists but is not exposed to Go/TS with the URL and cannot cancel navigation.
- Used the public WebViewNavigationCompleted event — it fires but does not include the URL.
- Worked around it on desktop by running a localhost callback listener to catch the redirect — works on desktop but is impossible on mobile (sandbox forbids port binding).

### System Details

```shell
- Wails v3: v3.0.0-alpha2.117
- Go: (fill your version, e.g. go1.22.x)
- OS / Platform: macOS / Windows / Linux (desktop) + iOS / Android (mobile)
- Frontend: (e.g. vanilla JS / React / etc.)
```

### Additional context

This is required for SSO / SAML / OAuth flows where the token is delivered via a post-login redirect or a session cookie. On mobile especially, a localhost listener is not an option, so in-WebView capture (navigation interception or cookie read) is the only viable path. A minimal, unified API across desktop and mobile would let the same auth code run everywhere.

comments.author: mortenolsrud
comments.body:
Hey, we ran into this exact problem in our Wails v3 app (OIDC PKCE auth on desktop + iOS + Android). Here's what worked for us:

**Short version: skip the WebView for auth entirely. Use the system browser + platform-specific callback capture.**

### Why system browser instead of WebView

RFC 8252 (OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps) recommends the system browser. It gives users SSO (shared cookies/sessions), and some IdPs like Google and Microsoft actively block WebView-based auth. No navigation interception or cookie APIs needed.

### How we did it

**Desktop (Windows/macOS/Linux):**
- Open the auth URL in the system browser via `platform.OpenBrowser(authURL)`
- Start a temporary localhost HTTP server listening for the callback
- IdP redirects to `http://localhost:PORT/callback?code=...`
- Extract the code, exchange for tokens, kill the server

This is what you already have as your desktop workaround. It's actually the "correct" approach, not a hack.

**Mobile (iOS/Android):**
- Localhost doesn't work in the sandbox, as you noted
- Instead: claimed HTTPS redirects via Universal Links (iOS) / App Links (Android)
- You register your app to handle a specific HTTPS URL (like `https://yourapp.example.com/auth/callback`)
- The IdP redirects there, and the OS routes it to your app instead of the browser
- Your Go code receives the callback URL through a channel

**What you need to set up:**
- iOS: Associated Domains entitlement + `apple-app-site-association` JSON file hosted on the domain

We need the macOS half of this for security. The content our window renders is sanitised by a model, so a link or a form can slip through and navigate the main frame off the app's origin. We want the host to refuse that.

On macOS there is no way to do it today. `webview_window_darwin.m` (checked on v3.0.0-beta.16 and beta.31) only implements the after-the-fact `WKNavigationDelegate` notifications, which carry no URL. There is no `webView:decidePolicyForNavigationAction:decisionHandler:`.

What would cover it is a callback that runs before the navigation, with the target URL and whether it is the main frame, and can allow or cancel it.

open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-c.title: [receiver/k8sevents] watch stalls forever without logging: RetryWatcher retries every second and the observer never re-lists
open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-c.body:
### Component(s)

receiver/k8sevents, internal/k8sinventory

### What happened?

## Description

The `k8s_events` receiver stops delivering events and never recovers, while the pod stays Running with no restarts and logs nothing at the collector's `WARN` log level (the retry loop described below logs only at klog V(1)/V(4)/V(5)). We found it on 8 of the 12 GKE clusters we checked, all running 0.158.0. Events kept being created on every affected cluster (`kubectl get events -A`), but the receiver's `otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records` stayed flat for days. Restarting the collector is the only remedy.

## Evidence from a stalled collector (7 days uptime)

- **Export side healthy.** `accepted_log_records` equals `exporter_sent_log_records`. The queue is empty, nothing is in flight, and the receiver reports no refused or failed records. So the pipeline is not blocking the receiver.
- **The apiserver keeps receiving the watch.** On one of the two apiserver replicas, `apiserver_request_total{resource="events",verb="WATCH",code="200"}` grew by about 60 per minute while `apiserver_watch_events_total{resource="events"}` did not move. A healthy cluster's apiserver showed no new events WATCH requests in the same minute. The counter stopped growing the moment the collector was restarted.
- **A goroutine dump (SIGQUIT)** shows the observer blocked on the result channel and the RetryWatcher cycling its 1 s retry loop:

```
github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/internal/k8sinventory/watch.(*Observer).doWatch(...)
	internal/k8sinventory@v0.158.0/watch/observer.go:326
github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/internal/k8sinventory/watch.(*Observer).startWatch.func2(...)
	internal/k8sinventory@v0.158.0/watch/observer.go:194
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait.UntilWithContext(...)

k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait.BackoffUntilWithContext(..., 0x3b9aca00 /* 1s */, ...)
k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait.NonSlidingUntilWithContext(...)
k8s.io/client-go/tools/watch.(*RetryWatcher).receive(...)
	k8s.io/client-go@v0.35.4/tools/watch/retrywatcher.go:295
```

## Why it never recovers

Since #45442 the receiver uses `internal/k8sinventory/watch`, which wraps client-go's `RetryWatcher` (`watch.NewRetryWatcherWithContext`). `RetryWatcher.doReceive` treats every outcome except `410 Gone`, Forbidden/Unauthorized and an unrecognised event type as "retry from `lastResourceVersion`":
- `io.EOF` and `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`
- a probable EOF or timeout
- a closed result channel
- 500 and 504 status errors
- any unknown status code

It logs those retries only at klog V(1)/V(4)/V(5). `Observer.doWatch` re-lists for a fresh resourceVersion only after a 410. So when the apiserver keeps ending the watch from the stored resourceVersion without a 410, the observer waits forever on a channel that never delivers. Nothing logs, and no metric shows it.

We could not capture what the apiserver returned; the stored resourceVersion lived only in the process. On GKE the events resourceVersions are timestamp-like (e.g. `1791811504203408999`), and a watch from a resourceVersion ahead of what the server serves hangs silently, so we suspect the stored resourceVersion ended up unservable on one replica. A watch from a valid resourceVersion delivered events immediately.

## Steps to Reproduce

We have no deterministic reproducer. It appeared on long-running collectors (days) on GKE regional clusters running Kubernetes 1.35.6-gke.1250001.

## Expected Result

When a watch delivers nothing for a long time, or keeps being re-established without progress, the observer re-lists and resumes. At minimum it should log a warning or expose a metric (watch restarts, last event age), so a stall can be detected.

## Actual Result

The receiver delivers nothing indefinitely. The process is healthy by every signal the collector exposes except `otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records` going flat.

## Possible fixes

- Bound the RetryWatcher: re-list after N consecutive restarts that brought no event, or after a configurable idle period.
- Use an informer (`cache.NewSharedInformer` / reflector), which re-lists on watch errors. The receiver used one before #45442.
- Expose watch-restart and last-event-timestamp metrics.

### Collector version

v0.158.0 (otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib image)

### Environment information

## Environment
GKE, Kubernetes 1.35, collector deployed by the OpenTelemetry Operator as a single-replica Deployment.

### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration

```yaml
receivers:
  k8s_events:
    auth_type: serviceAccount
processors:
  batch: {}
exporters:
  otlp_http:
    endpoint: http://loki-gateway/otlp
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [k8s_events]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp_http]
  telemetry:
    logs:
      level: WARN
```

### Log output

```shell
(none: the collector logs nothing before or during the stall)
```

### Additional context

The two give-up paths the observer does log (`Watch channel closed unexpectedly` at WARN, and a failed `getResourceVersion` at ERROR) were not hit: the stalled pods' logs were empty.
